speaker: alice
text: Okay, I think everyone is here. Thanks for joining the weekly status. Let's go quickly so we finish on time.

speaker: bob
text: Morning. Can you all hear me fine? My headset was acting up earlier.

speaker: carol
text: Yes, you sound fine. Loud and clear.

speaker: alice
text: Great. Quick recap of the sprint first. We closed eleven tickets last week and carried over four.

speaker: alice
text: The carried over ones are mostly the search indexing work, the onboarding redesign, and two small bugs in the settings page.

speaker: carol
text: Can I jump in on the settings bugs? One of them is mine, the dark mode toggle. It is fixed, I just have not merged it.

speaker: alice
text: Sure, please merge it today if you can. Bob, do you want to start with search indexing?

speaker: bob
text: Yes. So the indexer rewrite is about eighty percent done. The incremental updates work and the full rebuild works.

speaker: bob
text: What is left is the part that handles deleted documents. Right now a deleted document stays in the index until the nightly rebuild.

speaker: carol
text: Is that visible to users? Like, would they see a document that no longer exists?

speaker: bob
text: Yes, in the search results, for up to a day. The link would go to a not found page. It is ugly but not dangerous.

speaker: alice
text: Okay. Do we need to fix that before the next release, or can it wait?

speaker: bob
text: I would like to fix it. It is maybe two days of work, mostly testing, because the delete path touches a lot of places.

speaker: alice
text: Fine, let's plan for it. Anything blocking you on search?

speaker: bob
text: Not really. I need a review on the pull request for the query parser, though. It has been open since Tuesday.

speaker: carol
text: I can look at it this afternoon. Send me the link in the chat.

speaker: bob
text: Will do. Thanks.

speaker: alice
text: Sorry, I was writing that down. Carol, onboarding redesign next. Where are we?

speaker: carol
text: So I finished the new welcome screens, there are four of them now instead of seven. I tested them with five people last week.

speaker: carol
text: Four out of five finished the whole flow without help, which is better than before. The fifth person got stuck on the permissions step.

speaker: alice
text: What was confusing about the permissions step?

speaker: carol
text: The wording. It asks for access to notifications and to the camera in the same screen, and people did not know why we need the camera.

speaker: bob
text: We only need the camera for scanning, right? We could ask for it later, when they first scan something.

speaker: carol
text: Exactly my thinking. I will split it up and ask for the camera only when it is needed. I need to update the copy for that.

speaker: alice
text: Good. Do you need anything from engineering for that?

speaker: carol
text: A small thing. A way to check whether the permission was already granted, so we do not show our explanation twice.

speaker: bob
text: That exists already. I will send you the function name. It is one line.

speaker: carol
text: Perfect.

speaker: alice
text: Before the roadmap, let's talk about last Thursday. We had that failed deploy and I want to make sure we learned something from it.

speaker: bob
text: I can take that one. The short version is that the migration script ran twice. Our pipeline retried the step after a timeout, and the script was not safe to run a second time.

speaker: carol
text: What did users see while that was happening?

speaker: bob
text: A maintenance page for about twenty five minutes. Nobody lost data, we checked, but the profile pictures were missing until we restored them from the backup.

speaker: alice
text: Twenty five minutes is long. What took most of the time?

speaker: bob
text: Honestly, finding out what had happened. The logs for the migration step were in three different places and none of them told the whole story.

speaker: alice
text: So that is one action item. Put the logs in one place.

speaker: bob
text: Agreed. I would also like to make the migration script safe to run twice. Then a retry cannot hurt us, whatever the timeout does.

speaker: carol
text: Could we also have a smaller deploy window? I noticed we deploy everything on Thursday afternoon, which is when most customers are online.

speaker: alice
text: That is a fair point. What would you suggest?

speaker: carol
text: Early morning, before the east coast wakes up. Or at least not the afternoon.

speaker: bob
text: The earlier the better for me, but then someone has to be around. I do not want to be the only one watching the deploy at six in the morning.

speaker: alice
text: We can do a rotation. Let me think about how to set that up fairly, and I will propose something next week.

speaker: bob
text: While we are at it, the build is also slower than it was. It used to take eight minutes, now it takes closer to fourteen.

speaker: alice
text: Do we know why?

speaker: bob
text: Mostly the tests. We added a lot of end to end tests last month and they all run in sequence. I want to run them in parallel on four machines.

speaker: carol
text: That sounds expensive.

speaker: bob
text: A bit more per build, but the engineers waiting for it cost a lot more. I did the math, it pays for itself in about two weeks.

speaker: alice
text: Okay, you have my support. Write a short proposal with the numbers and I will approve it.

speaker: bob
text: Will do, thanks.

speaker: alice
text: Sorry, my other screen froze for a moment. Where were we? Right, the incident. Anything else on that?

speaker: carol
text: One question. Do we tell the customers what happened? A few of them asked in the support channel.

speaker: alice
text: Support already sent a short note on Friday. I think that is enough. If anyone asks for more, we send the full write up.

speaker: carol
text: Okay, I just wanted to be sure someone had done it.

speaker: alice
text: Okay, let me share my screen for the roadmap. Give me a second to find the right window.

speaker: alice
text: Can you see it now? The roadmap with the three columns.

speaker: bob
text: Yes, I can see it. The text is a bit small, though.

speaker: alice
text: Let me zoom in. Better?

speaker: bob
text: Better, thanks.

speaker: alice
text: So the middle column is what we committed to for this quarter. The file attachments feature is the big one in there.

speaker: carol
text: How far along is attachments? I have the designs ready but I have not heard much about the backend.

speaker: bob
text: The backend is mostly there. You can upload a file, it gets stored, and you can download it again. What I still need is the size check and the virus scan.

speaker: carol
text: For the upload dialog I need to write the error message for when a file is too big. So what is the maximum file size for uploads? Does anyone know the number?

speaker: alice
text: Hm. I thought we had decided that in the planning meeting. Bob, do you remember?

speaker: bob
text: I remember a long discussion, but I do not remember the outcome. I think it depends on the plan. Let me look it up later.

speaker: carol
text: Okay, I will put a placeholder in the design and fix it when someone tells me.

speaker: alice
text: Sounds good. Let's keep moving, we have a lot to cover.

speaker: bob
text: While we are on attachments, one side note. Uploading from the phone is slower than from the desktop, and I do not know why yet.

speaker: alice
text: Is that a problem for the release?

speaker: bob
text: Probably not, but I want to understand it. It might just be the mobile network in the office.

speaker: carol
text: I can test it on the home wifi tonight if that helps.

speaker: bob
text: That would help, yes. Thank you.

speaker: alice
text: Next, the customer feedback. Support sent me a summary of the top five requests from this month.

speaker: alice
text: Number one is still better search, which Bob is working on. Number two is dark mode, which Carol just fixed. Number three is the export to spreadsheet.

speaker: bob
text: The export is smaller than it sounds. A day, maybe a day and a half, if we only do the basic format.

speaker: alice
text: Great, let's add it to the list for next sprint. Number four is single sign on, and number five is the mobile app being slow.

speaker: carol
text: The mobile slowness is probably related to what Bob just said about the phone.

speaker: bob
text: Could be, yes. I will keep that in mind when I look at it.

speaker: alice
text: Next, the customer demo on the twentieth. It is with the big retail company that we have been talking to since the summer.

speaker: alice
text: I would like to show search, the new onboarding, and the attachments if they are ready. About thirty minutes in total.

speaker: carol
text: Who is doing the talking? I can walk through the onboarding, that is easy for me.

speaker: alice
text: I will do the intro and the search part. Bob, can you handle questions about the technical side?

speaker: bob
text: Sure. If they ask about security or hosting, I can answer that. If they ask about pricing, please do not look at me.

speaker: alice
text: Pricing is mine. Nobody else needs to say anything about it.

speaker: carol
text: I would like one dry run before the demo. Maybe the day before, with a customer like data set so the screens do not look empty.

speaker: bob
text: I can prepare the data. It would take me an hour or so to generate something realistic.

speaker: alice
text: Please do that. And let's agree now that we do not show anything that is not ready. If attachments are not done, we skip them and talk about them as upcoming.

speaker: carol
text: That seems wise. I would rather skip a feature than have a broken demo.

speaker: bob
text: Agreed. A crash during the demo is worse than a missing feature.

speaker: alice
text: Okay, now hiring. We have two open positions, one for backend and one for design, and I got the first batch of applications.

speaker: alice
text: There are about forty for backend and fifteen for design. I looked at them quickly and there are maybe six good ones in each group.

speaker: bob
text: Do you want me to help with the technical interviews? I can do one or two a week.

speaker: alice
text: Yes please. Let's start with the phone screens in two weeks. I will send you the list of candidates once I have narrowed it down.

speaker: carol
text: For the design role, I would like to give the candidates a small exercise instead of a long portfolio review. Something like a two hour task.

speaker: alice
text: Is a two hour exercise fair for them? Some people do not have the time.

speaker: carol
text: That is true. We could pay them for it, a small amount, or keep it to one hour and use it as a conversation starter.

speaker: alice
text: Let's go with one hour and no payment, but we make it optional. Anyone who prefers can send a portfolio instead.

speaker: carol
text: Okay, I like that. I will write up the exercise this week.

speaker: bob
text: A question about the backend role. Do we need someone with experience in search? Or is that too narrow?

speaker: alice
text: I would say experience in search is nice to have, but not required. Good general engineers can learn it.

speaker: bob
text: Good, because I do not want to filter out people who would be great. Learning the search part takes a few months at most.

speaker: carol
text: One more thing about hiring. Can we make sure the interview panel is not all the same kind of person? Last time it was three engineers and the candidate felt a bit outnumbered.

speaker: alice
text: Good point. I will make sure there is someone from design and someone from support on every panel.

speaker: carol
text: Thank you, that would be good.

speaker: alice
text: Okay, one more item before we finish. Some of the customers are asking when they get attachments. Do we have a date we can share?

speaker: carol
text: Support asked me this morning too. They want to tell customers it will be ready by Friday.

speaker: bob
text: Friday is not realistic. The scan and the size check are not done, and then there is testing.

speaker: alice
text: Right. So we can say it is coming soon, but no date yet. I will talk to support after this call.

speaker: carol
text: Okay. I will tell them not to promise a specific day.

speaker: alice
text: Last topic. The team offsite. We have the budget for it in the spring and I need to know whether people prefer a city trip or somewhere quiet.

speaker: bob
text: Somewhere quiet, please. I get tired of cities.

speaker: carol
text: I vote for the mountains. Somewhere with a lake would be perfect.

speaker: alice
text: Two for the mountains then. I will check some places and send a short list next week.

speaker: bob
text: Can we avoid anything that needs a long flight? Two hours by train is my limit.

speaker: alice
text: Noted. Train distance only.

speaker: carol
text: Before we finish, one thing about next week. I am out on Thursday for a doctor appointment, so if anyone needs design input, please ask on Wednesday.

speaker: alice
text: Thanks for telling us. Bob, are you around all week?

speaker: bob
text: Yes, all week. Except Friday afternoon, I leave early.

speaker: alice
text: Good. Let me summarize the action items. Bob, the delete path for search and the review of the parser pull request goes to Carol.

speaker: alice
text: Carol, merge the dark mode fix, split the permission screen and test the phone upload tonight. And I talk to support about the date and send the offsite list.

speaker: bob
text: And I send the function name for the permission check.

speaker: alice
text: Yes, that too. Anything else from anyone?

speaker: carol
text: Nothing from me.

speaker: bob
text: Nothing here either.

speaker: alice
text: Great, thanks everyone. Talk next week.
